question_html: Which section of the Companies Act, 2013 governs the issue of bonus shares?

options.A: Section 52
options.B: Section 62
options.C: Section 63
options.D: Section 53

answer_html: Answer: (C) Section 63 of the Companies Act, 2013 deals with the issue of bonus shares[cite: 14].
topic_text: Provisions of the Companies Act, 2013 for Bonus Issue

question_html: Out of which of the following reserves can fully paid-up bonus shares NOT be issued?

options.A: Capital Redemption Reserve Account
options.B: Revaluation Reserve Account[cite: 14]
options.C: Securities Premium Account
options.D: Free Reserves

answer_html: Answer: (B) Section 63 expressly states that no issue of bonus shares shall be made by capitalising reserves created by the revaluation of assets[cite: 14].

question_html: What is another term commonly used to refer to a bonus issue?

options.A: Sweat equity issue
options.B: Capitalisation of profits[cite: 14]
options.C: Right offering
options.D: Private placement

answer_html: Answer: (B) Bonus issue is also known as 'capitalisation of profits' or scrip issue[cite: 14].

question_html: Can a company once announce a bonus issue subsequently withdraw the same according to the Companies Act, 2013?

options.A: Yes, if approved by a special resolution.
options.B: Yes, prior to the allotment date.
options.C: No, a company which has once announced the decision recommending a bonus issue shall not subsequently withdraw the same[cite: 14].
options.D: Yes, with the permission of the National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT).

answer_html: Answer: (C) The company which has once announced the decision of its Board recommending a bonus issue shall not subsequently withdraw the same[cite: 14].

question_html: Can bonus shares be issued in lieu of dividend?

options.A: Yes, if authorized by Articles of Association.
options.B: No, bonus shares shall not be issued in lieu of dividend[cite: 14].
options.C: Yes, with the consent of 75% shareholders.
options.D: Only for preference shareholders.

answer_html: Answer: (B) Section 63(3) provides that bonus shares shall not be issued in lieu of dividend[cite: 14].

question_html: What is the limitation regarding the application of Securities Premium Account and Capital Redemption Reserve Account for bonus issues?

options.A: They can be used for paying up both unissued shares and unpaid calls on existing shares.
options.B: They can only be applied in the paying up of unissued shares to be issued as fully paid bonus shares and NOT for paying up unpaid amounts on existing shares[cite: 14].
options.C: They can be distributed as cash dividends.
options.D: They can be used to write off preliminary expenses only.

answer_html: Answer: (B) Securities premium and CRR may only be applied in the paying up of unissued shares and cannot be applied towards payment of unpaid amounts on existing shares[cite: 14].
topic_text: Application of Securities Premium and CRR

question_html: What happens to the net worth of a company immediately after the issuance of bonus shares?

options.A: It increases proportionately.
options.B: It decreases due to capitalization.
options.C: It remains unaffected / unchanged[cite: 14].
options.D: It equals total authorised capital.

answer_html: Answer: (C) While bonus shares increase the total number of shares, they do not increase the net worth of the company[cite: 14].

question_html: According to SEBI Regulations versus the Companies Act, 2013, how does the utilization of securities premium differ for bonus issues?

options.A: SEBI requires securities premium to be realized in cash, whereas the Companies Act has no such explicit restriction[cite: 14].
options.B: The Companies Act requires cash realization while SEBI does not.
options.C: There is no difference in rules between SEBI and Companies Act.
options.D: SEBI prohibits the use of securities premium entirely for bonus issues.

answer_html: Answer: (A) SEBI regulations mandate that securities premium be realized in cash, whereas under the Companies Act, 2013, unlisted companies can use securities premium not realized in cash[cite: 14].

question_html: Which of the following defaults will legally prevent a company from issuing bonus shares under Section 63(2)?

options.A: Default in payment of dividend on equity shares.
options.B: Default in payment of interest or principal in respect of fixed deposits or debt securities[cite: 14].
options.C: Default in payment of corporate tax for the previous year.
options.D: Default in filing annual returns with SEBI.

answer_html: Answer: (B) Section 63(2) prohibits bonus issue if the company has defaulted in payment of interest or principal on fixed deposits or debt securities, or statutory employee dues[cite: 14].

question_html: What must be done if the subscribed and paid-up capital exceeds the authorised share capital as a result of a bonus issue?

options.A: The bonus issue becomes void automatically.
options.B: A resolution shall be passed in a general meeting to increase the authorised capital[cite: 14].
options.C: Extra shares must be bought back by the company.
options.D: Approval must be taken from the High Court.

answer_html: Answer: (B) If subscribed capital exceeds authorised capital due to a bonus issue, a resolution must be passed to increase the authorised capital[cite: 14].

question_html: Alpha Company announced a bonus issue in the ratio of 2:3 (2 shares for every 3 shares held). Shareholder X holds 6,000 shares before the bonus issue. How many total shares will X hold after the bonus issue?

options.A: 4,000 shares
options.B: 6,000 shares
options.C: 10,000 shares[cite: 14]
options.D: 9,000 shares

answer_html: Answer: (C) Bonus shares = 6,000 / 3 x 2 = 4,000 shares. Total shares after bonus = 6,000 + 4,000 = 10,000 shares[cite: 14].

question_html: When partly paid-up shares are converted into fully paid-up shares by utilizing reserves for a bonus issue, which reserves are permitted to be used for this specific purpose?

options.A: Securities Premium Account only
options.B: Capital Redemption Reserve only
options.C: Free reserves (such as General Reserve or P&L), but NOT Securities Premium or CRR[cite: 14]
options.D: Revaluation reserves

answer_html: Answer: (C) Free reserves may be used for paying up amounts unpaid on shares, whereas securities premium and CRR cannot be applied towards payment of unpaid amounts on shares[cite: 14].
topic_text: Partly Paid Shares and Bonus Issue

question_html: What is the correct journal entry upon the sanction of a bonus issue utilizing General Reserve?

options.A: General Reserve A/c Dr. To Share Capital A/c
options.B: General Reserve A/c Dr. To Bonus to Shareholders A/c[cite: 14]
options.C: Bonus to Shareholders A/c Dr. To General Reserve A/c
options.D: Share Capital A/c Dr. To General Reserve A/c

answer_html: Answer: (B) Upon sanction of bonus issue, reserves are debited and Bonus to Shareholders Account is credited[cite: 14].

question_html: What is the final journal entry when bonus shares are actually allotted to shareholders?

options.A: General Reserve A/c Dr. To Equity Share Capital A/c
options.B: Bonus to Shareholders A/c Dr. To Equity Share Capital A/c[cite: 14]
options.C: Bank A/c Dr. To Bonus to Shareholders A/c
options.D: Share Capital A/c Dr. To Bonus to Shareholders A/c

answer_html: Answer: (B) Upon issue of bonus shares, Bonus to Shareholders Account is debited and Share Capital Account is credited[cite: 14].

question_html: Which of the following is a major effect of a bonus issue on a company?

options.A: Increase in cash and bank balances
options.B: Reduction in accumulated profits[cite: 14]
options.C: Increase in Earnings Per Share (EPS)
options.D: Increase in net worth

answer_html: Answer: (B) A bonus issue capitalizes profits/reserves, resulting in a reduction in accumulated profits and reserves[cite: 14].

question_html: How does a bonus issue impact the Earnings Per Share (EPS) and Book Value per share?

options.A: Both EPS and Book Value increase.
options.B: Both EPS and Book Value stand reduced[cite: 14].
options.C: EPS increases while Book Value decreases.
options.D: They remain completely unchanged.

answer_html: Answer: (B) Due to an increase in the number of shares without a corresponding change in net worth or earnings, effective EPS and Book Value per share stand reduced[cite: 14].

question_html: As per Section 2(43) of the Companies Act, 2013, what does 'free reserves' exclude?

options.A: General reserves
options.B: Credit balance of Profit and Loss account
options.C: Reserves created by unrealised gains, notional gains, or revaluation of assets[cite: 14]
options.D: Securities premium account

answer_html: Answer: (C) Free reserves exclude unrealised gains, notional gains, or revaluation of assets[cite: 14].

question_html: What is a 'Rights Issue'?

options.A: An issue of free shares to existing employees.
options.B: An issue of rights to existing shareholders to buy additional shares directly from the company in proportion to their existing holdings at a fixed time[cite: 14].
options.C: An issue of shares to the general public through an IPO.
options.D: A compulsory conversion of debentures by government order.

answer_html: Answer: (B) Rights issue is an issue of rights to existing shareholders entitling them to buy additional shares in proportion to their existing holdings[cite: 14].

question_html: According to Section 62(1)(a) of the Companies Act, 2013, what is the time limit specified within which a rights offer, if not accepted, shall be deemed to have been declined?

options.A: Not less than 7 days and not exceeding 15 days
options.B: Not less than 15 days and not exceeding 30 days[cite: 14]
options.C: Exactly 60 days
options.D: Not less than 30 days and not exceeding 90 days

answer_html: Answer: (B) The offer notice must specify a time not less than fifteen days and not exceeding thirty days from the date of the offer[cite: 14].
topic_text: Provisions of Section 62 for Right Issue

question_html: What does 'Renunciation of Right' mean?

options.A: Cancelling the company's registration.
options.B: The right of a shareholder to surrender his right to buy securities and transfer such right to any other person[cite: 14].
options.C: Refusing to accept dividends declared by the board.
options.D: Surrendering bonus shares back to the company.

answer_html: Answer: (B) Right of renunciation refers to the shareholder's right to surrender his right to buy securities and transfer it to another person[cite: 14].

question_html: How is the 'Value of Right' calculated?

options.A: Ex-right value minus Cum-right value
options.B: Cum-right value of share minus Ex-right value of share[cite: 14]
options.C: Issue price minus Face value
options.D: Market value plus Book value

answer_html: Answer: (B) Value of right = Cum-right value of share minus Ex-right value of share[cite: 14].

question_html: Which formula correctly represents the Ex-right value of shares?

options.A: (Cum-right value of existing shares - Rights shares x Issue Price) / (Existing shares + Right shares)
options.B: (Cum-right value of existing shares + Rights shares x Issue Price) / (Existing shares + Right shares)[cite: 14]
options.C: (Market value x Existing shares) / Right shares
options.D: Net worth / Total number of shares after issue

answer_html: Answer: (B) Ex-right value = [Cum-right value of existing shares + (Rights shares x Issue Price)] / (Existing shares + Right shares)[cite: 14].

question_html: A company offers new shares of ₹100 each at a 25% premium to existing shareholders on a 1-for-4 basis. The cum-right market price is ₹150. What is the ex-right market price of a share?
answer_html: Answer: (C) Ex-right value = (150 x 4 + 125 x 1) / (4 + 1) = 725 / 5 = ₹145 per share[cite: 14].

question_html: Based on the previous question (cum-right price ₹150, ex-right price ₹145, ratio 1 for 4), what is the value of a right?
answer_html: Answer: (B) Value of right = Cum-right price - Ex-right price = ₹150 - ₹145 = ₹5 per share[cite: 14].

question_html: Which situations are recognized under Section 62 where further shares can be issued WITHOUT offering them to existing shareholders?

options.A: ESOP schemes, private placement via special resolution, conversion of debentures/loans, and government direction in public interest[cite: 14].
options.B: Bonus issues and rights issues only.
options.C: Issue of shares at a discount to the general public.
options.D: Only when the company incurs net losses.

answer_html: Answer: (A) Section 62 recognizes four specific situations: ESOPs, special resolution placements, debenture/loan option conversions, and government directions in public interest[cite: 14].

question_html: How is Net Worth defined as per Section 2(57) of the Companies Act, 2013?

options.A: Total assets minus total outside liabilities including revaluation reserves.
options.B: Aggregate value of paid-up share capital and reserves created out of profits and securities premium, after deducting accumulated losses and deferred expenditure, excluding revaluation reserves[cite: 14].
options.C: Authorized capital plus general reserve minus bank overdraft.
options.D: Market capitalization of all issued equity shares.

answer_html: Answer: (B) Net worth means aggregate of paid-up capital and profit/securities premium reserves minus accumulated losses/deferred expenditure, excluding revaluation reserves[cite: 14].

question_html: What is Book Value of a share equal to?

options.A: Market price divided by total shares
options.B: Net worth (as per books) divided by Number of shares[cite: 14]
options.C: Face value plus securities premium
options.D: Paid-up capital divided by authorized capital

answer_html: Answer: (B) Book value of a share = Net worth as per books divided by the number of shares[cite: 14].

question_html: What is an advantage of a rights issue for a company?

options.A: It guarantees an increase in the market price of shares.
options.B: It acts as a natural hedge against issue expenses and is logistically much easier to handle than a public issue[cite: 14].
options.C: It entirely eliminates share capital dilution.
options.D: It avoids registration with regulatory bodies.

answer_html: Answer: (B) Right issue acts as a natural hedge against issue expenses and is logistically easier to handle than a public issue[cite: 14].

question_html: What is the accounting entry for the subscription of rights shares issued at a premium?

options.A: Bank A/c Dr. To Share Capital A/c
options.B: Bank A/c Dr. To Equity Share Capital A/c, To Securities Premium A/c[cite: 14]
options.C: Securities Premium A/c Dr. To Bank A/c
options.D: Equity Share Capital A/c Dr. To Bank A/c

answer_html: Answer: (B) Bank A/c is debited with total cash received, while Equity Share Capital A/c is credited with face value and Securities Premium A/c with the premium[cite: 14].

question_html: Are convertible debenture holders entitled to bonus shares in the same proportion as existing shareholders prior to conversion?

options.A: Yes, automatically upon announcement.
options.B: No, convertible debenture holders do not get bonus shares unless they have converted their debentures into shares before the record date[cite: 14].
options.C: Yes, if approved by a special resolution.
options.D: Only if mandated by the Securities and Exchange Board of India.

answer_html: Answer: (B) Convertible debenture holders are not equity shareholders until conversion, hence they do not receive bonus shares prior to conversion[cite: 14].

question_html: Can issued share capital including rights shares and bonus shares exceed the authorised capital of a company without amendment?

options.A: Yes, always.
options.B: No, issued share capital including bonus and rights shares must be within the authorised capital limit or the authorised capital must be increased[cite: 14].
options.C: Yes, with permission from auditors.
options.D: Only for private companies.

answer_html: Answer: (B) Issued share capital including rights and bonus shares cannot exceed authorised capital unless authorised capital is correspondingly increased[cite: 14].

question_html: What happens to the market price of a share after a rights issue?

options.A: It increases significantly due to higher capital.
options.B: It gets adjusted (decreases) to the theoretical ex-right market price[cite: 14].
options.C: It remains frozen at cum-right value.
options.D: It drops to the face value of the share.

answer_html: Answer: (B) Rights issue of shares results in adjustment/decrease of the market price per share in comparison to the pre-rights market price[cite: 14].

question_html: A company has 1,00,000 shares of ₹10 each (market value ₹46), and issues rights shares in a 1:10 ratio at an issue price of ₹31. What amount will be credited to Securities Premium Account upon subscription?
answer_html: Answer: (B) Rights shares = 1,00,000 / 10 x 1 = 10,000 shares. Premium per share = ₹31 - ₹10 (face value) = ₹21. Total Securities Premium = 10,000 x ₹21 = ₹2,10,000[cite: 14].
topic_text: Practical Calculation of Rights Issue Premium

question_html: What is a key governance benefit of a rights issue for existing shareholders?

options.A: It allows them to vote twice in annual general meetings.
options.B: It enables them to maintain their proportional holding and retain financial and governance rights, preventing dilution by outsiders[cite: 14].
options.C: It exempts them from paying future calls.
options.D: It guarantees fixed dividend payouts.

answer_html: Answer: (B) Rights issue enables existing shareholders to maintain their proportional holding and retain their financial and governance rights[cite: 14].

question_html: What happens if partly paid-up shares are outstanding on the date of allotment of a bonus issue?

options.A: Bonus shares can be issued without restriction.
options.B: The partly paid-up shares must first be made fully paid-up before bonus shares can be issued[cite: 14].
options.C: Bonus shares are issued only in proportion to the paid-up amount.
options.D: The board of directors can waive the requirement.

answer_html: Answer: (B) Section 63(2) mandates that partly paid-up shares, if any, must be made fully paid-up before issuing bonus shares[cite: 14].

question_html: Which of the following documents must be filed with the Registrar of Companies (RoC) along with a return of bonus issue?

options.A: A copy of the resolution authorizing the issue of bonus shares[cite: 14].
options.B: A detailed list of all employee salaries.
options.C: A valuation report from a registered valuer.
options.D: Bank statements for the past five years.

answer_html: Answer: (A) A return of bonus issue along with a copy of the resolution authorising the issue is required to be filed with the RoC[cite: 14].

question_html: A company decides to make a rights issue of 1 new share for every 2 shares held. Market value is ₹240, and the issue price is ₹120. What is the ex-right market price of the share?
answer_html: Answer: (B) Ex-right price = (240 x 2 + 120 x 1) / (2 + 1) = 600 / 3 = ₹200 per share[cite: 14].

question_html: Based on the previous question (cum-right price ₹240, ex-right price ₹200, ratio 1 for 2), what is the value of a right?
answer_html: Answer: (B) Value of right = Cum-right price - Ex-right price = ₹240 - ₹200 = ₹40 per share[cite: 14].

question_html: What is a disadvantage of a rights issue?

options.A: It legally increases company debt.
options.B: It invariably leads to dilution in the market value of the share of the company[cite: 14].
options.C: It requires approval from debenture trustees.
options.D: It prohibits future dividend distribution.

answer_html: Answer: (B) A primary disadvantage of a rights issue is that it invariably leads to dilution in the market value of the share[cite: 14].

question_html: Under Table F of Schedule I to the Companies Act, 2013, can free reserves be applied towards paying up amounts unpaid on existing shares?

options.A: No, free reserves can only be used for fully paid unissued bonus shares.
options.B: Yes, free reserves may be used for paying up amounts unpaid on shares held by existing shareholders[cite: 14].
options.C: Only if approved by the Central Government.
options.D: Only if the company has zero debt.

answer_html: Answer: (B) Table F allows the use of free reserves for paying up amounts unpaid on shares held by existing shareholders[cite: 14].
topic_text: Use of Free Reserves for Unpaid Calls

question_html: How is the market price of a company's shares before a rights issue officially termed?

options.A: Ex-right Market Price
options.B: Cum-right Market Price[cite: 14]
options.C: Book Value Price
options.D: Par Value Price

answer_html: Answer: (B) The market price existing before the rights issue is termed as Cum-right Market Price[cite: 14].

question_html: What does Section 62(3) state regarding debentures or loans containing an option to convert into equity shares?

options.A: Such conversion is illegal under Indian company law.
options.B: The restrictions of offering further shares first to existing shareholders do not apply to the increase in subscribed capital caused by the exercise of such conversion option[cite: 14].
options.C: They must be approved by SEBI prior to issuance.
options.D: They can only be converted at par value.

answer_html: Answer: (B) Section 62(3) exempts share capital increases resulting from pre-approved debenture/loan option conversions from standard rights offer rules[cite: 14].

question_html: Under Section 62(4), under what condition can the Government direct the conversion of debentures or loans into shares in a company?

options.A: If the company fails to pay dividends for two consecutive years.
options.B: If the Government considers it necessary in the public interest, notwithstanding if conversion terms were not originally included[cite: 14].
options.C: Only with the unanimous consent of all equity shareholders.
options.D: If the company's net worth becomes negative.

answer_html: Answer: (B) Section 62(4) empowers the Government to direct loan/debenture conversion into shares in public interest even without initial terms[cite: 14].

question_html: What is the general pricing policy for a rights offering compared to the current market price?

options.A: Always at a substantial premium to market price
options.B: Generally at a discount to the current market price to evoke positive response and reward shareholders[cite: 14]
options.C: Mandatorily equal to the book value
options.D: Fixed strictly at face value by law

answer_html: Answer: (B) Rights subscription price is generally at a discount to the current market price[cite: 14].

question_html: What action can the Board of Directors take after the expiry of the time specified in the rights offer notice (or upon earlier intimation of decline)?

options.A: They must cancel the entire capital increase.
options.B: They may dispose of the declined shares in such manner which is not disadvantageous to the shareholders and the company[cite: 14].
options.C: They must distribute them free of cost as bonus shares.
options.D: They can transfer them exclusively to the directors.

answer_html: Answer: (B) After the time expiry or decline, the Board may dispose of them in a manner not disadvantageous to shareholders and the company[cite: 14].

question_html: What is the primary psychological or market image effect of a bonus issue?

options.A: It is viewed negatively as a sign of cash shortage.
options.B: It is generally viewed positively by the market as a favorable corporate action[cite: 14].
options.C: It has zero impact on market sentiment.
options.D: It signals impending liquidation.

answer_html: Answer: (B) Bonus issue has an image enhancement effect, as the public and shareholders view it positively[cite: 14].

question_html: A company issues rights shares in the ratio of 1:10 at an issue price of ₹10 when its existing capital is 70,000 shares of ₹10 each. What is the journal entry amount upon subscription?
answer_html: Answer: (A) Rights shares = 70,000 / 10 x 1 = 7,000 shares at ₹10 each = ₹70,000 credited to Share Capital and debited to Bank[cite: 14].

question_html: Which governing authority's regulations specify that securities premium must be realized in cash for bonus issues by listed entities?

options.A: Reserve Bank of India (RBI)
options.B: Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI)[cite: 14]
options.C: Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority (IRDAI)
options.D: Ministry of Corporate Affairs (MCA)

answer_html: Answer: (B) As per SEBI Regulations, securities premium utilized for bonus issues should be realized in cash[cite: 14].

question_html: When converting partly paid-up shares into fully paid-up shares via bonus utilization, what is the sequence of journal entries?

options.A: First make final call due, then transfer from reserve to bonus account, then apply bonus money to call[cite: 14].
options.B: Directly credit share capital from P&L without calling money.
options.C: Issue fresh shares to public first.
options.D: Write off goodwill against capital redemption reserve.

answer_html: Answer: (A) The sequence involves providing for bonus from reserves, making the final call due, and adjusting the bonus money against the final call[cite: 14].
topic_text: Accounting for Partly Paid Shares Conversion

question_html: What is the theoretical ex-rights price representing in a company?

options.A: The historical cost of the asset.
options.B: A deemed value attributed to a company's share immediately after a rights issue transaction occurs[cite: 14].
options.C: The liquidation value of preference shares.
options.D: The dividend payout ratio.

answer_html: Answer: (B) Theoretical Ex-Rights Price is a deemed value attributed to a company's share immediately after a rights issue transaction occurs[cite: 14].
